-88.07180,43.14500.name: Froedtert & Medical College of Wisconsin, Reproductive Medicine Center
-88.07180,43.14500.desc: A fertility clinic reporting to the CDC's National ART Surveillance System. Medical director: Katherine Schoyer, MD. A fertility clinic is where human embryos are made, selected and stored, and where assisted reproduction happens, like IVF, ICSI, egg and sperm donation, freezing embryos and eggs for later. Reporting is required of every US clinic performing assisted reproduction, under the Fertility Clinic Success Rate and Certification Act, so this is close to a complete register rather than a list of members. What it records is cycles started, which is not the same as children born.

Approved for: ICSI — a single sperm injected into the egg; IVF with embryo transfer; embryo screening before transfer; insemination with donor sperm; insemination with the partner's sperm. A fertility clinic is where human embryos are made, selected and stored, and where assisted reproduction happens, like IVF, ICSI, egg and sperm donation, freezing embryos and eggs for later. Approval is compulsory in China and performing assisted reproduction without it is unlawful, so this list is a register rather than a directory of members. It names every approved institution in the country, which is more than almost any other state publishes. The address did not geocode, so this point sits at the centre of the province rather than at the institution.

-78.46780,-0.18070.name: Ministerio del Ambiente (Ecuador) — bioseguridad
-78.46780,-0.18070.desc: Ecuador wrote a prohibition on engineered seeds and crops into its constitution in 2008, then amended the position for research purposes. A constitutional ban is the strongest legal form this opposition has taken anywhere, and its subsequent softening shows what that form does and does not withstand.

-77.04300,38.90800.name: Washington Legal Foundation
-77.04300,38.90800.desc: Files briefs supporting manufacturers on preemption, expert evidence and the limits of regulatory authority, in cases including agrochemical claims. Amicus work of this kind is how a position enters the record without a party appearing to argue it, and the funders of such briefs are not always disclosed on the face of them.

-71.22900,42.44600.name: Revvity — Horizon Discovery
-71.22900,42.44600.desc: Supplies edited cell lines and CRISPR screening libraries to laboratories that do not make their own. Buying an engineered human cell line off a catalogue is ordinary practice and involves no biosafety filing by the purchaser, which is where a great deal of editing work actually begins.

-3.17900,51.48700.name: CryoArks
-3.17900,51.48700.state: Cardiff University — hubs in London and Edinburgh
-3.17900,51.48700.desc: A research-council-funded consortium of museums, zoos, universities and biobanks that built the United Kingdom's first comprehensive zoological biobank, linking millions of samples that were sitting in disconnected collections. Its two main storage hubs are the Natural History Museum in London and National Museums Scotland in Edinburgh; capacity runs to roughly a quarter of a million samples across freezers at minus eighty and liquid nitrogen. The point of the project is not storage but a common web portal and common standards, so a researcher can find out what exists. Two consequences worth holding: the material includes samples from wild populations and from species that are now extinct, and a stated aim is to reduce destructive sampling of permanent museum specimens by giving researchers something else to cut into.
